chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subbah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the gold with which children are ornamented, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to ornament his children and his women with gold and silver.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for children to wear gold jewelry in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the permissibility (jawaz) of children wearing gold, specifically citing the practice of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) who adorned his children and wives with both gold and silver. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a key counter-evidence to the view that gold is exclusively prohibited for males, establishing a distinction between the general prohibition for men and the allowance for children and women. The inclusion of 'wives' alongside 'children' further reinforces the permissibility for females, aligning with the broader consensus on female adornment.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Noman, from Abu Al Sabbah who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the gold which the children are ornamented with. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> used to ornament his<sup>asws</sup> children and his<sup>asws</sup> wives with the gold and the silver’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of children; if they can use gold as ornaments.
He (the Imam) said that Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, allowed his children and women to use gold and silver as ornaments.’”
